Scope and provenance. This preserved report starts from the fixed published trVAE representation and reproduces the downstream graph, aggregation, AutoK/GMM, enrichment, and proximity stages. It is not a claim of end-to-end representation equivalence. Every domain figure and downstream result in this report was generated from the completed compiled C++ CPU run. R Torch/CUDA remains available as an experimental alternative.

Static report. The installed HTML is self-contained scientific evidence. Its source is archival and expects the preserved result directory named in params$result_dir; it is not intended to rerun a full-data analysis during package installation.

This is the second CellCharterR tutorial and the complete scientific reproduction report. New users should first read the beginner workflow. The next tutorial demonstrates additional downstream analyses from the preserved C++ K=10 result.

1 Scope and artifact roles

This report consumes the completed compiled-C++ outputs. Earlier provisional outputs are not used here. The primary result is K=10, selected independently by the compiled C++ AutoK run over the predeclared range K=2 through K=20. The K=11 panel is a separate compiled C++ sensitivity fit corresponding to the tutorial’s requested resolution and seed 12345. The C++ and Python implementations use different initialization and random-number streams, so this does not claim seed-identical fitted parameters. Published H5AD cluster_cellcharter labels are not plotted as either R result.

role_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(manifest$roles, function(x) data.frame(
  role_id = x$role_id,
  k = x$k,
  seed = if (is.na(x$seed)) "NA (not an R fit)" else as.character(x$seed),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)))

Only BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 are displayed in maps. Enrichment and proximity statistics use all nine libraries. The full cell_type annotation is used for the log2 observed/expected dot plot with size_threshold=0.58, color_threshold=0.58, and the CellCharter v0.2.0 default clustered labels.

1.1 Full mouse-spleen before/after benchmark

format_duration <- function(seconds) {
  hours <- floor(seconds / 3600)
  minutes <- floor((seconds %% 3600) / 60)
  secs <- round(seconds %% 60)
  sprintf("%dh %02dm %02ds", hours, minutes, secs)
}

benchmark_table <- data.frame(
  implementation = c(
    manifest$benchmark$legacy$backend,
    manifest$benchmark$cpp$backend
  ),
  spatial_spots = format(manifest$benchmark$spots, big.mark = ","),
  features = manifest$benchmark$features,
  AutoK_rounds = manifest$benchmark$rounds,
  GMM_fits = manifest$benchmark$fits,
  observed_wall_time = c(
    paste0(">= ", format_duration(
      manifest$benchmark$legacy$elapsed_lower_bound_seconds
    )),
    format_duration(manifest$benchmark$cpp$elapsed_seconds)
  ),
  execution = c(
    paste0(manifest$benchmark$legacy$device, "; sequential K fits"),
    paste0(
      manifest$benchmark$cpp$workers, " workers x ",
      manifest$benchmark$cpp$threads_per_fit, " threads"
    )
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  benchmark_table,
  caption = "Observed timing for the same first five AutoK rounds (K=1 through K=21)"
)
Observed timing for the same first five AutoK rounds (K=1 through K=21)
implementation spatial_spots features AutoK_rounds GMM_fits observed_wall_time execution
R torch CUDA (sequential K fits) 707,474 40 5 105 >= 49h 47m 25s NVIDIA RTX A4000; sequential K fits
compiled C++ CPU (concurrent K fits) 707,474 40 5 105 0h 38m 20s 8 workers x 4 threads

For 707,474 spatial spots and 40 aggregated features, the compiled C++ run completed the same 105-fit, five-round comparison window at least 77.9 times faster. The legacy time is a conservative lower bound reconstructed from completed checkpoint timestamps, whereas the C++ duration was recorded by the runner. This is an observed workflow comparison, not a controlled microbenchmark: the backends use different initializers and numerical engines. The comparison is therefore evidence of the practical wall-time improvement, not a claim that both optimizers produce identical fitted parameters.

2 From input SPE to saved results

The full mouse-spleen analysis is deliberately not rerun while this report is rendered. The code below shows the public stages used to create the graph, in-memory neighborhood representation, AutoK fit, selected domains, and downstream statistics. The evaluated sections that follow load the corresponding precomputed artifacts and display their outputs.

full_spe <- readRDS("results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/representation/codex_sce.rds")

full_spe <- cellcharter_graph(
  full_spe,
  spatial = "spatial",
  sample_col = "sample",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  percentile = 99
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_aggregate(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  sample_col = "sample",
  output = "X_cellcharter",
  n_layers = 3L
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds",
  compress = FALSE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_v1/unused-no-checkpoints",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 0L,
  backend = "cpp",
  workers = 8L,
  threads_per_fit = 4L,
  checkpoint_mode = "none",
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L,
    tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6
  ),
  resume = FALSE
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain"
)
full_spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  permutation_mode = "cellcharter_v0.2.0"
)

saveRDS(
  full_spe,
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/downstream/codex_spe_complete.rds"
)

2.1 Optional resumable compiled C++ run

The measured 38-minute run above used checkpoint_mode = "none" to avoid all fit-checkpoint I/O. If interruption recovery is more important, use a new directory and checkpoint_mode = "round"; repeat this exact call with resume = TRUE after an interruption.

full_spe <- readRDS(
  "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/aggregation/spe_after_aggregation.rds"
)

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_resumable/autok",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  max_runs = 10L,
  convergence_tol = 0.01,
  seed = 0L,
  backend = "cpp",
  workers = 8L,
  threads_per_fit = 4L,
  checkpoint_mode = "round",
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L, tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6
  ),
  resume = TRUE
)

The resume call is deliberately identical to the original fit call. Changing the backend, seed, candidate range, or numerical settings creates a different fit contract and must use a new checkpoint directory.

2.2 Optional compact wrapper

For a compact dataset, cellcharter_workflow() composes the same stages. It is shown for completeness, but the staged version above is preferable for the full dataset because it exposes each durable checkpoint. If aggregation exceeds available RAM, add filepath = ... and retain that optional HDF5 file with the SPE.

full_spe <- cellcharter_workflow(
  full_spe,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  candidate_k = 2:20,
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_cpp_v1/unused-no-checkpoints",
  representation = "X_trVAE",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_col = "condition",
  aggregated = "X_cellcharter",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain",
  n_layers = 3L,
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  autok_args = list(
    backend = "cpp",
    workers = 8L,
    threads_per_fit = 4L,
    checkpoint_mode = "none",
    fit_args = list(
      max_iter = 100L, tolerance = 0.001,
      covariance_regularization = 1e-6
    )
  )
)

3 AutoK stability and K selection

The points are all saved neighboring-K Fowlkes–Mallows comparisons from the five repeated fits; the line is their mean. AutoK stopped before the requested maximum of ten runs because the final stability change was 0.00793, below the predeclared convergence_tol = 0.01. K=1 is shown as non-estimable because this criterion requires fitted solutions on both neighboring K values. K=10 is the independently selected global maximum. Other local peaks remain visible because stability is a resolution diagnostic, not a command to ignore biologically useful alternatives. K=11 is annotated as the predeclared tutorial-matched sensitivity on the neighboring stability shoulder.

knitr::include_graphics(manifest$autok_stability_plot)

Compiled C++ neighboring-K Fowlkes–Mallows stability for the full mouse-spleen analysis. K=10 is the independently selected primary resolution; K=11 is highlighted as the tutorial-matched sensitivity resolution, while other local peaks remain visible.

primary_k <- manifest$primary_k

Directed observed-minus-expected neighborhood enrichment for BALBc and MRL at the compiled C++ primary K=10 resolution. 

primary_nhood_table <- rbind(

)

4.4 Differential neighborhood enrichment in both display directions

Both panels reuse one sample-level permutation result (n_perms=100). A star marks directional empirical p <= 0.05; reversing the display negates only the effect and reuses the same permutation counts and p-values.

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL vs BALBc", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
plot_heatmap(
  primary_balbc_mrl$effect, "BALBc vs MRL", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_balbc_mrl$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)

Compiled C++ primary K=10 differential directed neighborhood enrichment in both MRL-minus-BALBc and BALBc-minus-MRL display directions. 

primary_diff_table <- matrix_long(primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL_minus_BALBc")
primary_diff_table$empirical_pvalue <- as.vector(primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue)
knitr::kable(primary_diff_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary differential heatmaps")

5 Standalone tutorial-matched K=11 sensitivity analysis

The C++ K=11 sensitivity was one standalone fit, not an AutoK selection and not the published H5AD labels. These are the exact historical settings used to generate its preserved labels:

full_spe <- cellcharter_cluster_fixed(
  full_spe,
  representation = "X_cellcharter",
  n_clusters = 11L,
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k11_sensitivity",
  checkpoint_dir = "results/CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_v2/tutorial_k11_standalone",
  seed = 12345L,
  fit_args = list(
    max_iter = 100L,
    tolerance = 0.001,
    covariance_regularization = 1e-6,
    num_threads = 4L
  ),
  predict_args = list(),
  fit_fun = cpp_gmm_fit,
  predict_fun = cpp_gmm_predict,
  resume = TRUE
)
k11_paths <- manifest$artifacts$TutorialK11
k11_map <- readRDS(k11_paths[["map_input"]])
k11_enrichment <- readRDS(k11_paths[["enrichment"]])
k11_nhood <- readRDS(k11_paths[["nhood"]])
k11_mrl_balbc <- readRDS(k11_paths[["differential_mrl_balbc"]])
k11_balbc_mrl <- readRDS(k11_paths[["differential_balbc_mrl"]])

5.1 BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 domains

6 Interpretation boundary

The R-selected AutoK K remains the only primary result. K=11 is a separately fitted tutorial sensitivity analysis. The published H5AD labels remain a separate reference artifact. Representation-learning equivalence is not claimed because the supplied trVAE representation is treated as immutable input. Spatial panels use ggspavis::plotCoords() on SpatialExperiment objects with the exact saved coordinates and labels. Pixel-level equivalence to Squidpy’s plotting stack is not claimed.
